text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Temp agencies and unions clash about proposed pay and conditions terms for temps. (p1)
- Supervisory boards of three of Noro's real estate funds resign en masse. (p1)
- Rabobank talks with two Belgian banks on Benelux alliance. (p1)
- Salaries of staff in the automation branch drop 2.9 pct from last year in spite of shortage of personnel. (p3)
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma holds onto idea of auctioning two new mobile phone frequencies. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Mayors in the Rotterdam region vote against the city's chief of police. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok vexed by finance minister Gerrit Zalm's criticism of Sweden's decision not take part in EMU. (p1)
- Market for single-premium insurance is booming. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Supermarkets in the Netherlands are in for a round of fierce competition as minimum prices will disappear next January. (p1)
- Pay and conditions agreement for Dutch PTT KPN unsettled again. (p7)
- ABN Amro's billion guilder loan to Russia's Gazprom put on ice. (p29)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Small investors angry at ABN Amro over its allocation policy for flotation of temp agency Vedior's. (p15)
TROUW
- Agreement between coalition parties and traffic minister on more competition in public transport is very flimsy. (p4)
